mainTopic: Overlapping נזירות vows: a chain of questions about whether the early days count, and a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about טומאה during a נזירות kept for a son.
overview: The גמרא is in the middle of a chain of 'if you say...' questions. Each new question assumes an answer to the one before it. The case is a person who vows to be a נזיר starting in twenty days, and also vows a נזירות starting right now. The second vow interrupts the first. The chain asks about a 100-day נזירות, a נזיר עולם, and a נזיר שמשון that can never be undone. It also asks about an unusual phrase, 'like משה on the seventh of אדר'. Then the גמרא resolves the very first question from a ברייתא: the first twenty days count, and he finishes the remaining eighty days later. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a man who pauses his own נזירות to keep one for his son. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether becoming טמא during the son's days also cancels his own earlier days. It depends on whether the two count as one long נזירות or two separate ones.

steps.title: Do the first twenty days count toward a hundred-day vow?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we accept that with a short (30-day) נזירות, the ten leftover days are not counted. Then what about a 100-day נזירות, where eighty days are left at the end?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that with a short נזירות the leftover ten days don't count for him, then what about a 100-day נזיר? Since he has eighty days at the end, do the first twenty count for him or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question that builds on an assumed answer to an earlier question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a 30-day נזירות, he keeps 20 days, is interrupted by the second vow, and only 10 days are left afterward. We assume those 10 are too few to finish properly, so the first 20 don't count. With a 100-day נזירות, 80 days are left afterward, which is plenty. So maybe here the first 20 do count.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say: the formula for a follow-up question built on an assumed answer
A short נזירות (the standard thirty days)

phrases.english: If you say, regarding a short naziriteship,
phrases.notes: This picks up the earlier case: a regular thirty-day נזירות from now, while another נזירות is set to start in twenty days.

phrases.english: since it is only ten days that are left over,
those ten are not counted for him,
then certainly, a nazir of one hundred days,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ תְּמָנִין יוֹמִין לְבַסּוֹף,
phrases.english: since he has eighty days at the end,
are they counted for him, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a chain of questions that began before this section, building on an assumed answer about a short נזירות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the first twenty days of a 100-day נזירות count, given that eighty days remain after the interruption.

steps.title: What about a permanent נזיר starting now?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the first twenty days do take effect in the 100-day case. Then what if the vow from now is to be a נזיר עולם?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say they do take effect: if he said 'I am a נזיר after twenty days, and from now a נזיר עולם', what is the law? Does it take effect on him or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves up the chain. It assumes the first days count, and asks about a permanent נזירות starting now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 100-day case, the first twenty days count because he can finish the rest later. A נזיר עולם never ends, so there is no 'later' in which to finish it. That makes it unclear whether the permanent vow can begin during those first twenty days.

phrases.english: And if you say they do take effect:
if he said: "I am hereby a nazir after twenty days
and from now a permanent nazir," what is the law?
does it take effect on him, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes a 'yes' answer to step 1 and pushes the question to a נזירות that has no end.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a נזיר עולם vow from now takes effect during the twenty days before the other נזירות begins.

steps.title: What about a נזיר שמשון, which cannot be released?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the permanent vow from now takes effect because the later vow (after twenty days) can be released through a חכם. Then what about a נזיר שמשון after twenty days, which can never be released?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that here it takes effect because it is possible to ask for release: if he said 'I am a נזיר שמשון after twenty days, and from now a plain נזיר', what is the law? Here it is not possible to ask for release, so does it take effect or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא climbs one more step. It assumes a reason for the previous answer, then tests a case where that reason is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason for the נזיר עולם case is that he could ask a חכם to undo the vow set to start in twenty days. Then the נזירות from now could continue without a break. In the new case, the vow after twenty days is a נזיר שמשון, which cannot be undone this way. So the plain 30-day נזירות from now might have no way to be completed, and the גמרא asks whether it takes effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask a חכם to release a vow
A נזיר modeled on שמשון, with special rules
A plain נזיר with no number given (thirty days)

phrases.english: If you say: here,
since it is possible to ask for release, it takes effect:
phrases.notes: He could ask a חכם to undo the vow that starts in twenty days, so the נזירות from now can run without a break.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי נְזִיר שִׁמְשׁוֹן לְאַחַר עֶשְׂרִים יוֹם
phrases.english: if he said: "I am hereby a Samson-nazir after twenty days
and from now a plain nazir," what is the law?
Here it is not possible to ask for release,
does it take effect, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר: הָכָא כֵּיוָן דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְאִיתְּשׁוֹלֵי חָיְילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes step 2 is answered 'yes' because release is possible, then tests a case where release is impossible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the plain נזירות from now takes effect when the later vow is a נזיר שמשון, which can never be released.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'it is possible to ask for release' is not part of the person's vow. It is the reason the גמרא is assuming for the previous answer.

steps.title: Does saying 'like משה on the seventh of אדר' make one a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: A separate question: if someone says 'like משה on the seventh of אדר', what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'like משה on the seventh of אדר', what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a different kind of question, this time about whether an unusual phrase counts as a נזירות vow at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question here is not about overlapping days. It is about wording: does this odd expression mean the person is taking on נזירות? The גמרא leaves the question open here.

keyTerms.meaning: Like משה on the seventh of אדר

phrases.english: If he said, "Like Moses on the seventh of Adar," what is the law?
phrases.notes: The seventh of אדר is the day משה passed away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks away from the chain of overlapping-days questions to ask a separate question about wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the expression 'like משה on the seventh of אדר' counts as accepting נזירות.

steps.title: The first question is resolved: the first twenty days count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the 100-day question from a ברייתא. He counts twenty days, then thirty for the second vow, then eighty to finish the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve the first of them: 'I am a נזיר after twenty days, and from now one hundred days.' He counts twenty, then thirty, then eighty to complete the first נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the very first question in the chain (step 1) using a teaching that states this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the first twenty days of the 100-day נזירות count. He pauses for the thirty-day נזירות, then completes the remaining eighty. So when enough days are left at the end, the early days are not wasted. The later questions in the chain are not answered here.
steps.whatToRemember: In a 100-day נזירות interrupted by another נזירות, the first twenty days count. He keeps twenty, then thirty for the other vow, then the last eighty.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the base question of the chain. The other questions that build on it (נזיר עולם, נזיר שמשון, the משה phrase) stay open in this section.

phrases.english: Resolve from them the first one:
phrases.notes: 'The first one' is the 100-day question from the start of this section.

phrases.english: "I am hereby a nazir after twenty days
and from now one hundred days":

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מוֹנֶה שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: he counts twenty, and afterward counts thirty,
and afterward counts eighty
in order to complete the first naziriteship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the later questions to answer the first question (step 1).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first twenty days count. He counts 20, then 30 for the second vow, then 80 to complete the 100-day נזירות.

steps.title: Becoming impure during the son's nazirite days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether טומאה during the son's נזירות also cancels the days already counted for his own נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure during the days of his son's naziriteship: רבי יוחנן says it cancels. ריש לקיש says it does not cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a man who stopped his own נזירות in the middle to keep a נזירות for his newborn son. It brings a מחלוקת about what happens if he becomes טמא during the son's days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who becomes טמא must start his count again. Here there are two נזירות, one paused in the middle and one he is keeping now. רבי יוחנן says the טומאה wipes out even the days he already counted for his own נזירות. ריש לקיש says it only wipes out the son's נזירות, and his earlier days still count.

keyTerms.meaning: He became ritually impure, for example through contact with a dead body
During the days of the נזירות he took on because of his son
Cancels. The טומאה undoes the days already counted
Does not cancel. The earlier days still count

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the son's נזירות has to start over. The argument is only about the days he already counted for his OWN נזירות before he paused.

phrases.english: If he became impure during the days of his son,
phrases.notes: This means the days of the נזירות he took on for his son, which he is keeping in the middle of his own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: It cancels.
Reish Lakish says: It does not cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְמָא בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: סוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of overlapping vows and the ברייתא and returns to the משנה's case of a נזירות for a son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: טומאה during the son's נזירות cancels his own earlier days too. ריש לקיש: it cancels only the son's נזירות.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן sees both נזירות as one long נזירות. ריש לקיש sees them as two separate ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it cancels because it is one long naziriteship. ריש לקיש says it does not cancel because his own naziriteship is separate and his son's is separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds the way he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that since the son's נזירות sits in the middle of his own, the whole thing is one long stretch of נזירות. So טומאה anywhere in it restarts everything. ריש לקיש says they are two separate נזירות, so טומאה in the son's part only affects the son's part.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument comes down to one question: are the two נזירות one long unit (רבי יוחנן) or two separate units (ריש לקיש)? That decides how far the טומאה reaches.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'one long נזירות' versus 'separate נזירות' is a clear way to understand how vows that overlap or are nested inside each other relate to each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says it cancels —
because it is one long naziriteship,
Reish Lakish says it does not cancel —
because his own naziriteship is separate,
and that of his son is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר סוֹתֵר — חֲדָא נְזִירוּת אֲרִיכְתָּא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the מחלוקת from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן treats the nested נזירות as one long unit. ריש לקיש treats them as two separate units.
